scenario: An app intercepts and forwards incoming SMS one-time passcodes to a remote number (a documented SMS-relay fraud pattern).

supported_findings: The app registers an exported SmsInterceptReceiver for incoming SMS combined with SEND_SMS, and strings reference OTP pattern matching and SMS forwarding.
This combination of permissions, an exported broadcast receiver for incoming SMS, and forwarding-related strings is consistent with a design capable of relaying one-time passcodes to a third party.
No traffic_log, call log, or SMS log entries are present in this case confirming any specific message was intercepted or forwarded.
unsupported_claims_to_watch_for: Any claim that a specific one-time passcode was actually intercepted or forwarded -- this case contains no log evidence of the capability being exercised.
Any claim that a specific person's account was compromised as a result.
Any claim naming the destination number or service the OTPs were allegedly forwarded to -- no such value appears in this case's artifacts.
